items.grounds: Re-derived from bytes both ways. The row's primary hook verifies at byte tier: תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה closes colon A of oshb:Prov.15.8 (its final word carries ETNAHTA U+0591) and תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה opens oshb:Prov.15.9; the contiguous-skeleton construction stands in 11 verses book-wide (sweep.py --skel, verse count: Prov.3.32, 11.1, 11.20, 12.22, 15.8, 15.9, 15.26, 16.5, 17.15, 20.10, 20.23) and Prov.15.8|Prov.15.9 is the sole adjacent pair among them, the seam sharing two word-bound skeleton tokens (תועבת and יהוה). The finding's target is the second ground, and it also verifies. The wicked-genitive template is byte-real - construct heads stand before the wicked-token in זֶ֣בַח רְ֭שָׁעִים at oshb:Prov.15.8 and דֶּ֣רֶךְ רָשָׁ֑ע at oshb:Prov.15.9 - but it distinguishes nothing at this seam. Word-bound skeleton sweeps, object named, verse counts: the singular wicked-token רשע stands in 36 verses and the plural רשעים in 35 verses book-wide (70 verses carry one or the other), exactly as filed; the row's two forms are different word-bound tokens (plural at 15:8, singular at 15:9), so the template shares no wicked-token across the seam at any word-bound tier; the identical construct-plus-wicked pattern stands two verses earlier at oshb:Prov.15.6, וּבִתְבוּאַ֖ת רָשָׁ֣ע (byte tier), and again in the same chapter at oshb:Prov.15.28, וּפִ֥י רְ֝שָׁעִ֗ים; and the wicked-token itself forms 7 adjacent same-token pairs elsewhere in the book (singular at 10:24|10:25 and 11:7|11:8; plural at 10:6|10:7, 10:27|10:28, 11:10|11:11, 12:5|12:6, 12:6|12:7), none of which the corpus clusters on that ground. A construction that recurs across most of the collection and binds no other adjacent pair cannot supply 'the construction ground binding the pair into one boundary decision', and the row names no swept object or digit for it. Not load-bearing: the tocevat-YHWH hook carries the cluster alone and the row's device_notes already call the repeated phrase the driver, so the filed medium is the right severity for a defective secondary warrant. Both sides weighed at byte tier: the preceding row's closing verse oshb:Prov.15.7, שִׂפְתֵ֣י חֲ֭כָמִים יְזָ֣רוּ דָ֑עַת וְלֵ֖ב כְּסִילִ֣ים לֹא כֵֽן, shares no word-bound skeleton token with oshb:Prov.15.8, and the row's closing verse oshb:Prov.15.9 shares none with the following row's opening verse oshb:Prov.15.10, מוּסָ֣ר רָ֭ע לְעֹזֵ֣ב אֹ֑רַח שׂוֹנֵ֖א תוֹכַ֣חַת יָמֽוּת; the governing device (a catchword straddling exactly one seam) decides both edges, and the rows spanning Prov.15.7 and Prov.15.10 state the same empty seams, so the boundary is coherent on all three rows. The proposed field repair is byte-supported and endorsed as a proposal only: demote the template to disclosed texture with its object and digits named (36 and 35 word-bound verses; the same construct pattern at oshb:Prov.15.6) and leave the tocevat-YHWH hook as the single driver.

Both sides of the seam the finding concerns, spliced at byte tier: the preceding row's closing verse oshb:Prov.15.30, מְֽאוֹר עֵ֭ינַיִם יְשַׂמַּֽח לֵ֑ב שְׁמוּעָ֥ה ט֝וֹבָ֗ה תְּדַשֶּׁן עָֽצֶם; this row's opening verse oshb:Prov.15.31, אֹ֗זֶן שֹׁ֭מַעַת תּוֹכַ֣חַת חַיִּ֑ים בְּקֶ֖רֶב חֲכָמִ֣ים תָּלִֽין. Prov.15.30 is the verse immediately before Prov.15.31, so the row's stated ground for excluding it ('not adjacent to this chain') is false as a positional claim whatever the writer meant by it. The seam actually holds on a different object, which the corpus already carries at the preceding row: the hearing root appears as the noun שְׁמוּעָ֥ה at oshb:Prov.15.30 and as the participle שֹׁ֭מַעַת at oshb:Prov.15.31, two distinct word-bound skeleton tokens (שמועה stands in 1 verse book-wide, שמעת in 3: Prov.15.31, 20.12, 25.12), and the two verses share no word-bound skeleton token at all. The chain the row builds re-derives as filed: תוכחת is a shared word-bound skeleton token at Prov.15.31|Prov.15.32 (תּוֹכַ֣חַת against תּ֝וֹכַ֗חַת, equal at accent-stripped tier, distinct at byte tier), and מוסר at Prov.15.32|Prov.15.33 (מ֭וּסָר absolute against מוּסַ֣ר construct, equal at skeleton tier only); word-bound the noun תוכחת stands in 8 verses and מוסר in 23 verses book-wide, and Prov.15.31|Prov.15.32 and Prov.15.32|Prov.15.33 are the only adjacent pairs among them, so the two-link chain is byte-real and the boundary decision is unaffected by the defect. The row's front seam was also weighed: oshb:Prov.15.33 ends the chapter and shares no word-bound skeleton token with oshb:Prov.16.1, לְאָדָ֥ם מַֽעַרְכֵי לֵ֑ב וּ֝מֵיְהוָ֗ה מַעֲנֵ֥ה לָשֽׁוֹן, whose divine-name form וּ֝מֵיְהוָ֗ה is a different word-bound token from יְ֭הוָה. The defect is a byte-false statement inside the row's own back-seam defense, not load-bearing because the boundary survives on the true ground: confirm at medium. The proposed field repair (restate the exclusion on the distinct-word-bound-token ground and disclose the root-level echo as texture) is byte-supported and endorsed as a proposal only; it also brings the row into line with the preceding row's stated rejection of the same pairing.

Re-derived from bytes, object named first. The row's two verses at byte tier: oshb:Prov.16.10, קֶ֤סֶם עַֽל שִׂפְתֵי מֶ֑לֶךְ בְּ֝מִשְׁפָּ֗ט לֹ֣א יִמְעַל פִּֽיו; oshb:Prov.16.11, פֶּ֤לֶס וּמֹאזְנֵ֣י מִ֭שְׁפָּט לַֽיהוָ֑ה מַ֝עֲשֵׂ֗הוּ כָּל אַבְנֵי כִֽיס. The auditor's byte facts all verify: בְּ֝מִשְׁפָּ֗ט and מִ֭שְׁפָּט are distinct word-bound skeleton tokens (במשפט in 4 verses book-wide: Prov.16.10, 18.5, 24.23, 29.4; bare משפט in 12: Prov.2.8, 8.20, 12.5, 13.23, 16.8, 16.11, 17.23, 19.28, 21.7, 21.15, 28.5, 29.26), the seam Prov.16.10|Prov.16.11 shares no word-bound skeleton token, the bare form stands two verses earlier as מִשְׁפָּֽט at oshb:Prov.16.8, and the 16:11 token re-sweeps at 1 verse byte tier and 13 accent-stripped including Prov.16.10. The inference built on them does not verify. First, the match is not the hazard catalog's contained-substring trap (a different lexeme sharing letters, as כמה inside חכמה): the bet on the 16:10 form is a proclitic preposition on the same noun, so the two verses share one content lexeme, mishpat, in prefixed and bare forms - a lexical catchword under the campaign's own definition, not a false hit. Second, the corpus does not apply a word-bound-only seam metric: the adjacent row spanning Prov.16.12-Prov.16.15 rests on the royal noun across the word-bound-empty seam Prov.16.13|Prov.16.14 (מְ֭לָכִים plural against מֶ֥לֶךְ singular), the row spanning Prov.18.18-Prov.18.19 rests on a bare form against a waw-prefixed qere, and the row spanning Prov.15.31-Prov.15.33 links מ֭וּסָר to מוּסַ֣ר at skeleton tier only; the rows spanning Prov.16.1 and Prov.16.9 refused the 16:1-16:9 envelope because the only recurring token there is the divine name, which they discount as non-content (the bare word-bound token alone stands in 70 verses book-wide), plus three fully empty seams - a different test from the one this row faces. Third, the mishpat object is more distinctive than either the row or the finding states: the contiguous-skeleton sweep returns 20 verses book-wide (sweep.py --skel, verse count) with exactly two adjacent pairs, Prov.2.8|Prov.2.9 in the lectures and Prov.16.10|Prov.16.11, so within the Solomon collection Prov.10.1-Prov.22.16 this seam is the sole adjacent recurrence of the lexeme among its 12 verses there; and the owner-ruled strategy itself names a kings run at 16:10-15 as a cluster candidate, so it contemplates 16:10 and 16:11 inside a multi-verse unit. The cluster therefore has byte-grounded cohesion named in its rationale, which is what the collection's granularity law requires, and the filed high (a load-bearing defect: a cluster with no byte cohesion) is not supported. What is defective, and medium: the rationale presents the object as 'the shared noun' with only a within-span digit ('sweep: 2 consecutive verses'), never states that the two forms are distinct word-bound tokens, names no tier, and omits the book-wide and collection digits that actually distinguish the pair; and strongest_rejected_alternative rejects only the forward extension and never states or rejects the collection's default single_proverb atomization, the mandated rival for every proverb_cluster row. Downgrade to medium. Both sides of every seam the proposal touches, at byte tier: the preceding row's closing verse oshb:Prov.16.9, לֵ֣ב אָ֭דָם יְחַשֵּׁ֣ב דַּרְכּ֑וֹ וַֽ֝יהוָ֗ה יָכִ֥ין צַעֲדֽוֹ, shares no word-bound skeleton token with oshb:Prov.16.10; the following row's opening verse oshb:Prov.16.12, תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת מְ֭לָכִים עֲשׂ֣וֹת רֶ֑שַׁע כִּ֥י בִ֝צְדָקָ֗ה יִכּ֥וֹן כִּסֵּֽא, shares none with oshb:Prov.16.11 (the verb עֲשׂ֣וֹת and the noun מַ֝עֲשֵׂ֗הוּ are different lexemes of one root); the interior seam carries the mishpat lexeme. The governing rule is the collection's catchword law, and by it the outer edges are empty either way while the interior seam is the one place in the collection where the lexeme recurs in adjacent verses. Span ruling: decline_proposal. Retiring the pair is not byte-compelled: it would dissolve a byte-true catchword on the strength of a word-bound-only metric the corpus applies nowhere else, and it would leave מֶ֑לֶךְ at oshb:Prov.16.10 as an unpaired royal-noun verse directly before the kings run, reopening the seam that the rows spanning Prov.16.10-Prov.16.11 and Prov.16.12-Prov.16.15 currently argue coherently (each states from bytes why 16:11 carries no royal noun and why 16:10 is bound forward by mishpat). The auditor's alternative remedy is the byte-supported one and is endorsed as a field-repair proposal only: re-cut the rationale to name the object as one lexeme in prefixed and bare forms that are distinct word-bound tokens, carry the digits above (4 and 12 word-bound; 20 contiguous with two adjacent pairs book-wide, one in this collection), and state and reject the single_proverb atomization on those grounds. For owner triage: a one-link catchword cluster is the class the strategy expects to hold at lower confidence, so the row's medium sits at the top of its honest range.

The mark facts verify against the inventory: pmarks_Prov.json records one paseq seg at Prov.16.10 and one at Prov.16.11 (single witness, WLC), the row cites them without an intra-verse position claim and with the single-witness qualifier, and the parashah inventory records no petuchah or setumah seg in chapters 15, 16 or 18, so no span-relevant parashah disclosure is owed at any row in this slice (a symmetry fact, not counterevidence). The tier claim does not verify: the inventory's marks_note assigns TIER-3 WEAK corroboration to the petuchah/setumah layer only, its paseq_note records the paseq inventory as a count-only seg layer with no tier at all, and the owner-ruled strategy lists paseq among disclosure objects, not evidence tiers; calling the paseq 'a corroborating tier-3 signal' imports the parashah tier onto a layer that carries none, a tier overclaim of the class the campaign treats as a defect regardless. The function claim fails independently: a paseq is a separator between two words inside one verse, so one seg inside oshb:Prov.16.10 and another inside oshb:Prov.16.11 say nothing about whether the two verses cohere, in either direction; the row could cite them only as span-touching disclosure. Not load-bearing on its own, since the row names the mishpat lexeme as the driver and the paseq as corroboration only: confirm at medium (a defective mark claim that is not alone load-bearing). The proposed field repair - keep the two segs as untiered, count-only, single-witness disclosure bearing on nothing in the boundary decision - is byte-supported and endorsed as a proposal only. both_sides_assessed is false because this is a mark-tier and mark-function item that concerns no seam; the row's seams are weighed from both sides at M8-Prov-218#p38-1.

Spliced at byte tier from the staged extract (word positions are the extract's space-delimited tokens; the extract is maqaf-free): oshb:Prov.18.6, שִׂפְתֵ֣י כְ֭סִיל יָבֹ֣אֽוּ בְרִ֑יב וּ֝פִ֗יו לְֽמַהֲלֻמ֥וֹת יִקְרָֽא, is 7 words with ETNAHTA U+0591 on word 4, בְרִ֑יב, so colon B is words 5-7 and the verse closes on יִקְרָֽא; oshb:Prov.18.7, פִּֽי כְ֭סִיל מְחִתָּה ל֑וֹ וּ֝שְׂפָתָ֗יו מוֹקֵ֥שׁ נַפְשֽׁוֹ, is likewise 7 words with the ETNAHTA on word 4, ל֑וֹ, colon B words 5-7, closing on נַפְשֽׁוֹ. The forms the row says close each verse, וּ֝פִ֗יו and וּ֝שְׂפָתָ֗יו, are word 5 of 7 in both and OPEN colon B; the row's two 'closes' claims are byte-false positional claims, exactly as filed. The device itself survives and is byte-stronger than the row states: the head noun כְ֭סִיל is codepoint-identical at word 2 of both verses (accent included) and is the seam's only shared word-bound skeleton token, and the body-part terms reverse across the pair - שִׂפְתֵ֣י then וּ֝פִ֗יו against פִּֽי then וּ֝שְׂפָתָ֗יו - so the chiasm is real and the defect is confined to its positional description. Count-object note for the repair: word-bound כסיל stands in 22 verses book-wide with 5 adjacent pairs (17.24|17.25, 18.6|18.7, 26.4|26.5, 26.5|26.6, 26.10|26.11), so the repeated head noun alone is not what distinguishes this pair; the chiastic reversal is, and the re-cut should say so. Not load-bearing: confirm at medium. Both sides weighed at byte tier: the preceding row's closing verse oshb:Prov.18.5, שְׂאֵ֣ת פְּנֵי רָשָׁ֣ע לֹא ט֑וֹב לְהַטּ֥וֹת צַ֝דִּ֗יק בַּמִּשְׁפָּֽט, shares no word-bound skeleton token with oshb:Prov.18.6, and oshb:Prov.18.7 shares none with the following row's opening verse oshb:Prov.18.8, דִּבְרֵ֣י נִ֭רְגָּן כְּמִֽתְלַהֲמִ֑ים וְ֝הֵ֗ם יָרְד֥וּ חַדְרֵי בָֽטֶן; the governing device (a two-verse chiasm on a repeated head noun) straddles only the interior seam, and the rows spanning Prov.18.5 and Prov.18.8 both reject clustering across these edges, so the three rows are coherent. The proposed field repair (replace 'closes' with 'opens the second colon with', add the true closing words and the word-4 etnahta as the divider, and name the byte tier for the head-noun identity) is byte-supported and endorsed as a proposal only.

Spliced at byte tier: oshb:Prov.18.10, מִגְדַּל עֹ֭ז שֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֑ה בּֽוֹ יָר֖וּץ צַדִּ֣יק וְנִשְׂגָּֽב; oshb:Prov.18.11, ה֣וֹן עָ֭שִׁיר קִרְיַ֣ת עֻזּ֑וֹ וּכְחוֹמָ֥ה נִ֝שְׂגָּבָ֗ה בְּמַשְׂכִּיתֽוֹ. The headline claim fails at every collation tier: the construct heads differ outright (מִגְדַּל against קִרְיַ֣ת), the strength noun is bare עֹ֭ז against suffixed עֻזּ֑וֹ, and the seam Prov.18.10|Prov.18.11 shares no word-bound skeleton token at all, so there is no tier at which 'the exact same construct-noun-of-strength phrase' is run twice. Sweeps re-derived with the object named: the word-bound skeleton עז stands in 6 verses book-wide (Prov.14.26, 18.10, 18.19, 21.22, 30.25, 31.25), including Prov.18.10 and excluding Prov.18.11, exactly as filed - with the count-object caveat that the skeleton blends the noun with the pausal adjective at oshb:Prov.30.25 (עָ֑ז, qamets), so the noun-only digit is 5; the suffixed word-bound form עזו stands in 2 verses (Prov.10.15, 18.11). No tier is named anywhere in the row for an exact-identity claim, which the campaign's tier discipline requires. Not load-bearing: the row's next sentence states the true object (strength noun and exalted form recurring across the seam at root level), the exalted root is the pair's distinctive byte object (contiguous skeleton שגב in 3 verses book-wide, Prov.18.10|Prov.18.11 the sole adjacent pair), and the antithesis the row describes is real, so the defect is an identity overstatement inside a sound warrant: confirm at medium. Both sides weighed at byte tier: the preceding row's closing verse oshb:Prov.18.9, גַּ֭ם מִתְרַפֶּ֣ה בִמְלַאכְתּ֑וֹ אָ֥ח ה֝֗וּא לְבַ֣עַל מַשְׁחִֽית, shares no word-bound skeleton token with oshb:Prov.18.10, and oshb:Prov.18.11 shares none with the following row's opening verse oshb:Prov.18.12, לִפְנֵי שֶׁ֭בֶר יִגְבַּ֣הּ לֵב אִ֑ישׁ וְלִפְנֵ֖י כָב֣וֹד עֲנָוָֽה; the rows spanning Prov.18.9 and Prov.18.12 each state the absence of a catchword across these edges, so the edges are coherent on all three rows. The proposed re-cut (state the strength root as a root-level recurrence, bare at word 2 of 18:10 against suffixed at word 4 of 18:11, with tier and digit, and delete the exact-phrase sentence) is byte-supported and endorsed as a proposal only, with the noun/adjective caveat above attached to its digit.

Both facts verify at byte tier: words 1-4 of oshb:Prov.18.11, ה֣וֹן עָ֭שִׁיר קִרְיַ֣ת עֻזּ֑וֹ, are codepoint-identical to words 1-4 of oshb:Prov.10.15, ה֣וֹן עָ֭שִׁיר קִרְיַ֣ת עֻזּ֑וֹ, where colon B is מְחִתַּ֖ת דַּלִּ֣ים רֵישָֽׁם and no refuge saying precedes; the contiguous-skeleton sweep of those four words returns exactly 2 verses (Prov.10.15, 18.11), word-bound קרית 2 verses (the same two) and contiguous קרית 3 (adding מִקִּרְיַת at oshb:Prov.18.19, the near-repeat inside this chapter). So the colon the row's rejected alternative calls 'built to invert the first's claim word-for-word' is a stock colon of the collection, and no word-for-word inversion exists in any case (the heads and the strength forms differ, as ruled at the companion item). The actual byte device is the one the finding identifies: the exalted root, וְנִשְׂגָּֽב closing oshb:Prov.18.10 (word 8 of 8) against נִ֝שְׂגָּבָ֗ה at word 6 of oshb:Prov.18.11, contiguous skeleton שגב in 3 verses book-wide (Prov.18.10, 18.11, 29.25 - the last as יְשֻׂגָּֽב) with Prov.18.10|Prov.18.11 the sole adjacent pair, rendered “and are safe” (web:Prov.18.10) and “an unscalable wall” (web:Prov.18.11), verbatim against the staged WEB; together with בְּמַשְׂכִּיתֽוֹ it carries the true-refuge against imagined-refuge antithesis. The rival rejection therefore rests on a mischaracterized device and omits a byte fact that directly undercuts it; the cluster is not destroyed, so the defect is not load-bearing: confirm at medium. Both sides weighed (the same edges as the companion item): oshb:Prov.18.9 shares no word-bound skeleton token with oshb:Prov.18.10 and oshb:Prov.18.11 none with oshb:Prov.18.12, and the adjacent rows state the same, so the pair's edges are coherent; the interior seam carries the exalted-root recurrence and the root-level strength echo. The proposed field repair is byte-supported and endorsed as a proposal only, with one qualification: making the exalted-root recurrence the primary warrant and the strength root a disclosed secondary echo is right, the 10:15 disclosure and the mirrored oshb:Prov.10.15 reference follow the corpus's refs-mirror rule, and the rewritten rival must reject independence on the adjacent-recurrence ground rather than on any built-to-invert claim, which the bytes cannot support.

Spliced at byte tier: oshb:Prov.18.18, מִ֭דְיָנִים יַשְׁבִּ֣ית הַגּוֹרָ֑ל וּבֵ֖ין עֲצוּמִ֣ים יַפְרִֽיד; oshb:Prov.18.19, אָ֗ח נִפְשָׁ֥ע מִקִּרְיַת עֹ֑ז ומדונים וּ֝מִדְיָנִ֗ים כִּבְרִ֥יחַ אַרְמֽוֹן, where ומדונים is the inline unpointed ketiv and וּ֝מִדְיָנִ֗ים the pointed qere (pmarks_Prov.json: one ketiv/qere note at Prov.18.19, single witness). The auditor's tiers and digits verify: מִ֭דְיָנִים and the qere are distinct word-bound skeleton tokens (the qere adds a conjunctive waw and carries a different accent set, geresh muqdam plus revia against dehi), the word-bound form מדינים stands in 8 verses book-wide (Prov.6.14, 18.18, 21.9, 21.19, 23.29, 25.24, 26.21, 27.15; 6 of them themselves qere readings beside an inline ketiv) and the waw-prefixed form in 1 (Prov.18.19), the seam shares no word-bound skeleton token, and identity holds at the contiguous-skeleton tier, where the sweep returns 9 verses with Prov.18.18|Prov.18.19 the sole adjacent pair - a digit the row does not carry and which strengthens it. The row's 'repeated unchanged' is therefore a verbatim-class claim with no tier named that is false at byte, accent-stripped and word-bound tiers, and 'exact-repetition catchword' reads the same way. Adversarial correction to the finding: 'the exact same inflected form' is not false as morphology - both tokens are the masculine plural absolute of one noun, and a proclitic waw is not an inflection - so the finding overstates by one claim. Severity is downgraded to low: the object (one plural noun recurring across the seam), the qere-built warrant with the ketiv stated and the single-witness qualifier, and the sole-adjacent-pair status are all byte-sound; the row quotes both forms, so the waw and the accent difference are visible to any reader; what is missing is the tier at which 'unchanged' is true (contiguous skeleton) - a tier-naming disclosure shortfall inside a sound warrant, not a defective warrant claim.
